summary: Round 8, decomposition only -- no code, no tests, so the lens is whether the rows will produce tests that fail when the production code is wrong. The round-7 major is rendered faithfully and every factual claim in it verified against the code: Checkpoint.pods is a length-prefixed sorted UTF-8 String (Checkpoint.encode), VERSION is a constant 0 and decode compares against it, so qualifying the key is genuinely a no-format-change, and the failure direction stated (a real replay ACCEPTED TWICE against a pre-upgrade checkpoint, not a real commit suppressed) is correct. The production reviewer's correction is absorbed correctly and verified independently: SegmentCommit carries the rendered segmentKey (podShortId + per-pod sequence) and RunCommit carries absolute firstOffset, so only flushSeq is absent from the chain. Four minors, all of the name-the-thing kind; per review.md minors-land and the rule-12 tail about rounds 7-10 on prose commits, none buys a round 9.

findings.title: "all three goldens round-trip" -- the goldens are still unnamed and the count is not recoverable
findings.failure_scenario: The sentence's subject is Checkpoint.pods, and there is exactly ONE checkpoint golden: format/src/test/resources/golden/checkpoint-v0.bin, read by GoldenCheckpointTest. The directory holds seven .bin goldens (chain-continue-v1, chain-delta-batched-v1, chain-delta-v0, chain-seal-v1, checkpoint-v0, segment-v0, segment-v1), so 'three' is neither the checkpoint set nor all of them; the only reading that yields three is checkpoint-v0 plus the two CommitDelta goldens, which the sentence does not say. A session at M4.10b checking the claim greps for three checkpoint goldens, finds one, and cannot tell whether the evidence was wrong or its scope was. This is the unpinned-number failure baselines/review.txt records twice for this task family. Separately, the goldens are the WEAK half of the evidence: they are fixed bytes and a writer-side key qualification cannot touch them, so they round-trip trivially. The load-bearing fact is that the pod key is written as putUvarint(len) + UTF-8 bytes and sorted as a String, which is what makes any longer key format-neutral -- and it is not cited.
findings.suggested_fix: Name them (golden/checkpoint-v0.bin, chain-delta-v0.bin, chain-delta-batched-v1.bin) or drop the count and cite the length-prefixed encoding instead.

findings.title: The chain-carries-pod-attribution correction is stated without the consequence that keeps it from becoming a prescription
findings.failure_scenario: Verified correct: SegmentCommit.segmentKey is the rendered SegmentKey, which carries podShortId and the per-pod sequence, and RunCommit carries an absolute firstOffset -- so the chain can in principle both DETECT and ANSWER a replay of the uncheckpointed tail keyed on segmentKey alone, without flushSeq. The 'bound to pin, not close' framing therefore survives, but for a different reason than before: the tail is not an information gap, it is a cost gap. The added sentence states the fact and stops. backlog-notes.md's own header instructs a session to read the entry for the ONE task it picks, so a session picking M4.10d reads 'SegmentKey puts podShortId and a per-pod sequence inside the segment key that every SegmentCommit carries, and each RunCommit carries the original offsets' with no adjacent statement that reading them means a backwards walk -- and implements the chain scan that rounds 4-5 already rejected ('one GET and no growth'), reinstating the unbounded replay M4.9 removed. The prohibition exists, but only in M4.10b's third property, one row away.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the half-clause: '-- and reading them means the backwards walk M4.10b's third property forbids, so the tail is a BOUND to pin, not an unanswerable gap.'

findings.title: The row calls deleting the tripwire a rule-5 inversion, but no gate can see that deletion -- measured
findings.failure_scenario: Measured against scripts/test_integrity.py: doesNotContainKey matches no pattern in the STRENGTH table and scores 0 (the (2) row matches a literal '.contains', which '.doesNotContainKey' does not contain). Removing the assertion from CheckpointWriterContentTest#theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll leaves the method's score at 2, identical to before -- so check-test-integrity.sh is silent on exactly the deletion the row names as forbidden. A session at M4.10d that finds the tripwire inconvenient deletes it, every gate stays green, and the anchor the row calls its corroborating half is gone with no trace. The row currently reads as though a rule owns this; nothing does.
findings.suggested_fix: Say the gate is blind here (the strength table scores doesNotContainKey at 0), so the refusal is the reviewer's, not a script's -- or raise a harness row to add the doesNotContain* family to the table.

findings.title: M4.10d names one of the thirteen source files carrying an 'until M4.10' promise, and the split is what stranded the other twelve
findings.failure_scenario: Measured: 24 bare 'M4.10' references across 13 files -- 6 main, 6 test, 1 testFixtures. Two are test-lane and invisible to every gate. FakeSequencer's javadoc binds itself: idempotency 'lands here in the same commit as the real behaviour so the two cannot drift'. After this split no commit will ever carry the subject M4.10, so the binding now has no commit to attach to, and if M4.10d lands without touching the fixture then FakeSequencer accepts a replayed (podId, flushSeq) while production refuses it -- every test written through the fake passes while the real seam behaves differently, which is the divergence the fixture's own javadoc says is worse than no fake at all. FakeSequencerTest:179 is worse still: 'the fake does not dedup on (podId, flushSeq) and neither does the real sequencer until M4.10' is an as() DESCRIPTION, not an assertion, so when it becomes false nothing fails and nothing prints. M4.10d's row names only CheckpointWriterContentTest. The M4.10a entry in baselines/review.txt records this exact failure on this exact task -- fixing one copy of a fact and missing its duplicates -- and M4.45 records a reviewer finding another instance by grepping *.java where the author's grep covered only docs. Mitigating, and why this is a minor: M4.10 still RESOLVES to the split banner, which points at b/c/d, so a session grepping the ID is redirected rather than stranded.
findings.suggested_fix: One clause in M4.10d: this row owns the in-tree promissory notes -- 24 references in 13 files -- including FakeSequencer's javadoc and FakeSequencerTest's as() text, which no gate can see. Also worth naming there: inverting doesNotContainKey falsifies the method name theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll, its in-method comment, and CheckpointWriter.java:52-54, whose javadoc points AT that test.

notes: Round-7 major, rendering checked rather than accepted: correct in substance and in direction. The property is unconditional (a plain bullet in M4.10b's list, not gated on the ADR's answer), it names the pre-change checkpoint explicitly, it states why the hazard survives 'no formats change' -- verified: Checkpoint.VERSION is a constant 0, decode refuses only version != VERSION, and pods keys are putUvarint(len)+UTF-8 sorted as Strings, so 'poda' -> 'poda@e7' changes no byte layout -- and it states the opposite failure direction correctly: a recovered map keyed 'poda' never matches a lookup on 'poda@e7', so the replay is admitted twice rather than a genuine commit being suppressed. The only soft spot is the golden citation, filed above.

Which of the round-7 minors must land HERE, given this commit builds nothing: strictly, none -- all four are one-clause additions and review.md minors-land says fixing them on a pass is permitted and usually wrong, because the next round's surface is the prose the fix adds. If any are taken, take the two whose text is inside THIS diff (the golden count at :235 and the M4.10d ownership clause at :281), because they are cheapest to state while the rows are being written and most expensive to notice later. The tripwire-gate blindness and the falsified method name are properly M4.10d's, at the moment the inversion is actually performed.

Tier and layer: nothing to report. No test changed, and the anchor M4.10d chooses (CheckpointWriter over MemoryBinStore with a frozen ticker) is already the right tier -- no socket, no wall clock, no real object store.
